answer: Each new identity must pass an in-person check by an accredited verifier, who inspects a government ID and issues one credential bound to a key. Verifiers stake funds slashed if an audit proves a false issuance, and each epoch a sample is re-checked. A wharf stall or a remote vertex follows the same rule, so a farm cannot mint hundreds of accounts from one room: every fake needs a paid visit, travel, and a verifier risking its stake. A whisper of collusion can be reported. Limits: rural coverage is thin, small bribery is possible, and people without ID are excluded, so appeals are needed.
